tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description begins with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill for...'), explicitly enumerates a wide range of trigger symptoms/contexts (avails not filling, slate, ADS timeouts, VAST parse failures, specific error codes, Channel Assembly states, etc.) so the agent can match on symptoms even when the user doesn't name MediaTailor directly, and explicitly carves out non-applicable scope (handoffs to other skills). It is dense but stays within a reasonable paragraph length and is implementation-light, focused on symptoms/user-observable problems rather than internal mechanics.
tests.evidence: Use this skill for AWS Elemental MediaTailor SSAI (server-side ad insertion) and Channel Assembly. Use for ad symptoms: avails not filling, slate or source content instead of ads, empty VAST/VMAP, ADS timeouts or errors...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but all content is domain-specific: MediaTailor-specific dimension names, log event types, metric names, and non-obvious operational facts. There is no explanation of generic concepts the agent would already know (e.g., no 'what is HLS' or 'what is an API').
tests.evidence: "LogConfiguration.PercentEnabled: defaults to 0, and anything below 100 samples sessions, so a missing log line is not evidence of health." — this is specific, non-obvious domain knowledge, not general explanation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed tables (metric catalogs, log event catalogs, error tables) are explicitly pushed to references/ files and only summarized or pointed to inline. Conditional branches (e.g., the fill-rate three-way split) stay at a decision-logic level rather than embedding full lookup tables.
tests.evidence: "Table: [Step S1: Configuration and logging precheck](references/lookup-tables.md#step-s1-configuration-and-logging-precheck). Load it when you run this step." shows detailed tables are offloaded to references.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ is linked via markdown link syntax somewhere in the body.
tests.evidence: Links found for all 8 files: channel-assembly-checklist.md, channel-assembly-procedure.md, lookup-tables.md, playback-errors-and-limits.md, report-outlines.md, ssai-fill-behavior.md, ssai-log-catalog.md, ssai-metric-reference.md, e.g. "[references/ssai-log-catalog.md](references/ssai-log-catalog.md)"

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a specific triggering condition or purpose, not a generic 'for details' phrase.
tests.evidence: "load the \"Observability preconditions\" section of [references/ssai-log-catalog.md](references/ssai-log-catalog.md) when you need the exact field, default, cap or documented trap"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference file paths use relative 'references/filename.md' format with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (CLI pagination flags, log query patterns, exact DATA GAP wording) are prescriptive, while diagnostic reasoning (fill-rate branch analysis, symptom-to-step mapping) explains the why and leaves room for judgment.
tests.evidence: "Omit --max-results and all pagination flags so the SDK auto-paginates; passing caps causes errors" is prescriptive for a fragile CLI quirk, while "Pursue the dominant SkippedReason.*" gives reasoning-based guidance.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where tool/approach choices exist (e.g., metrics-first vs logs, which log group to start with), a clear default/order is given with escalation paths rather than an undifferentiated list.
tests.evidence: "Metrics-first reasoning is the rule: even in a total log gap, CloudWatch metrics support real conclusions; logs add per-session and per-ad detail on top."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable investigative method (symptom routing table, diagnostic branches, DATA GAP protocol) applicable to any MediaTailor resource, not a one-off instance task.
tests.evidence: "Investigate a single MediaTailor capability instance: either a playback configuration (SSAI) or a linear channel (Channel Assembly)" frames a reusable procedure, and the symptom-to-step table generalizes across many symptoms.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive, explicit gotchas treatment: the observability-off-by-default section, scope boundary warnings, and the 'Before presenting' checklist all document concrete non-obvious traps.
tests.evidence: "This is the dominant design fact for MediaTailor and the most common reason an investigation cannot reach a conclusion." and "A cached personalized manifest produces \"everyone gets the same ads\" with every MediaTailor metric healthy."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides an explicit output structure (Step F) and points to a dedicated report-outlines.md reference for templates, satisfying the need for structured output guidance.
tests.evidence: "Use the matching report outline (SSAI or Channel Assembly) in [references/report-outlines.md](references/report-outlines.md) when compiling the report; load it at this step only."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the Step F section describes required fields in prose and defers the actual template structure to references/report-outlines.md.
tests.evidence: "Use the matching report outline (SSAI or Channel Assembly) in [references/report-outlines.md](references/report-outlines.md) when compiling the report" shows the template is offloaded, not inlined.
